chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Amr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah swore upon Himself that he shall not sit upon the cushions of Paradise the one who allows others into his behind. So I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'So-and-so is intellectual and understanding, inviting people unto himself. Allah has afflicted him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Does he do that in the congregational mosque?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So, does he do it upon the door of his house?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So where does he do it?' I said: 'When he is alone.' He said: 'So Allah has not afflicted him. This one is doing it for pleasure. He shall not sit upon the cushions of Paradise.'

key_terms.يُؤْتَى فِي دُبُرِهِ: Allows others into his behind (anal intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between public and private anal intercourse in Shia jurisprudence regarding exclusion from Paradise?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between anal intercourse performed for public display or social status versus private pleasure, noting that the former is a greater affliction. The scholar notes that doing it in the mosque or one's door signifies a desire for public recognition, whereas doing it when alone is merely for personal gratification, thus sparing one from the specific exclusion from the 'cushions of Paradise' (namāqir al-jannah). This highlights the Shia emphasis on the intention and context of bodily acts in determining spiritual consequence.
